preconditions.description: The number of acorns n is a positive integer within the specified bounds.
The input sequence a has exactly 2n - 1 elements.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= n for x in a)
preconditions.description: Each element in the sequence a is either 0 (illegible) or a valid acorn index between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'no' or (stdout == 'yes' and len(output_tour) == 2 * n - 1)
postconditions.description: If no valid Euler tour exists, output 'no'. Otherwise, output 'yes' followed by a valid Euler tour of length 2n - 1.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and all(1 <= x <= n for x in output_tour)
postconditions.description: Every element in the output Euler tour is a valid acorn index between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and output_tour[0] == output_tour[-1]
postconditions.description: The first and last elements of the output Euler tour are the same.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and all(a[i] == 0 or a[i] == output_tour[i] for i in range(len(a)))
postconditions.description: Every element in the output Euler tour matches the corresponding element in the input sequence a, where 0 in a is treated as a wildcard.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and all(x in output_tour for x in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: Every acorn index from 1 to n appears at least once in the output Euler tour.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and all(output_tour[i] != output_tour[i + 1] or (i == 0 and output_tour[i] == output_tour[i + 1]) for i in range(len(output_tour) - 1))
postconditions.description: Consecutive elements in the output Euler tour are different, except for the first and last elements which must be the same.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and len(set((output_tour[i], output_tour[i+1]) for i in range(len(output_tour)-1))) == n - 1
postconditions.description: The output Euler tour must correspond to a valid tree structure, meaning the multiset of consecutive node pairs (edges) must contain exactly n-1 unique edges (each traversed exactly twice, except for the start/end node).

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'yes' and all(output_tour.count(x) <= 2 or (output_tour.count(x) == 3 and x == output_tour[0]) for x in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: Each acorn is collected at most once, except for the start/end acorn which may be collected one additional time (i.e., no acorn is collected more than twice, except the start/end acorn which may be collected three times).
